title: The lonely runner conjecture for eight and nine runners: a kernel-checked proof
description: A formalization in Lean 4 with Mathlib of the lonely runner conjecture for eight and nine runners: 1/8 <= ML(v) for every seven positive integer speeds and 1/9 <= ML(v) for every eight positive integer speeds. The two Lean theorems have no hypothesis and depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (no sorry, no native_decide). The proof uses a formalization of the seven-runner case of Barajas and Serra, reductions to finite certificates for 27 primes (eight runners) and 36 primes (nine runners), generated by Rust programs and checked by the Lean kernel, and a bridge from the eight-runner theorem to the nine-runner theorem. Both cases are known from computer-assisted proofs in the literature, so no new case of the conjecture is claimed; the contribution is a machine-checked proof of both. The archive contains 18,139 Lean modules of a 25,988-module import closure (the other modules, generated data, are listed with sha256 and regenerated by scripts), the Rust generators and a reproduction entry point. The 36 nine-runner libraries were built separately over several days with restarts, the 27 eight-runner libraries were built outside lake in September 2026, and the final assembly (three modules) was elaborated once with raw lean over these restored and staged libraries, which were not recompiled in that run; no from-scratch rebuild in one run was made. The library contains superseded modules with unused axioms and sorry stubs that the final theorems do not depend on (checked by #print axioms). The Lean modules, the Rust generators and the first draft of the paper were produced by an AI system (Claude, Anthropic); the questions, the research directions and the decision to formalize these statements came from Vico Bonfioli. The Lean kernel, not a human reader, checks the proofs. The paper has not been peer reviewed. Comments in many Lean modules and the first line of generated modules were edited for the public release; Lean declarations and proofs are unchanged, and the checksums in the archive are those of the shipped files.
